title: Holiday Ad Photos and Videos for Gift Season | AIVideosUGC
description: Make holiday ad photos and videos from one product photo. Add confirmed dates, prices or offers after download, then reuse the scene as campaigns change.
h1: Create Holiday Ad Photos and Videos Fast
lead: Turn one product photo into a gift-ready scene, then add the shipping date after you download.

faq.q: How many credits does a holiday photo or video use?
faq.a: A photo uses 24 credits. Video uses 24 credits for 6 seconds, 40 for 10, 60 for 15, or 120 for 30. The cost shows before you start, and a failed job returns those credits.

faq.q: Can I add music or captions to the holiday clip?
faq.a: Add them after download in your editor. AIVideosUGC does not put music or captions in the file. Use a track you have the rights to play.

faq.q: Can I make holiday scenes for a whole catalog at once?
faq.a: No. Each product photo is its own job. Start the next product when you are ready.

faq.q: Can the scene use a real customer or a celebrity?
faq.a: No. People in the scene are generated. They are not real customers, real celebrities, or people you filmed.

faq.q: What happens to the visual after the holiday ends?
faq.a: You keep the file you downloaded. Change the date or the offer in your editor and reuse the scene for the next seasonal push.

faq.q: Can I start from my everyday product photo?
faq.a: Yes. Upload the clear photo you already use and describe a seasonal setting. The product itself should stay easy to recognize.

faq.q: How do I put an order-by date on the ad?
faq.a: Type it in your editor after download. Keeping the date off the generated image lets you change it as the cutoff gets closer.

faq.q: Can I run the download as a paid holiday ad?
faq.a: Yes. The file has no AIVideosUGC watermark. You can use it in seasonal ads, subject to each platform's current ad rules.

faq.q: Can I make Mother's Day product ads the same way?
faq.a: Yes. Describe a Mother's Day table or gift scene instead of a winter one, and add that occasion's date after download.

items.t: Lift the set out of the tissue
items.d: They upload the gift-set photo and ask for hands lifting it from a box. The order-by line is typed later, so a moved cutoff does not force a new scene.

items.d: They keep the coat's color and shape, with a person standing next to an open gift. That person is generated, not a hired customer.

items.d: They download the candle-and-ribbon scene once. For the next push they only change the offer line in the editor.
